beats.text: Now, remember the *Dial*?
After the war, the federal government ran Texas for a while.
Formerly enslaved men got the vote, and almost all of them voted for one party,
the party of Lincoln, the *Republicans*.
For a brief moment, Texas had Republican government.
In 1870, Edmund J. Davis became governor.
He was a Texan who had fought for the Union.
Black Texans were elected to the legislature for the first time.
Many white Texans saw Davis's government as an *occupation*.
It had a state police, higher taxes, and the backing of federal troops.
His supporters saw something else, the first government in Texas that tried to
protect the rights of Black citizens.
Either way, it did not last.
In the 1873 election, the Democrat Richard Coke beat Davis by about *two* to one.
Davis refused to leave at first.
For a few days, Texas had two rival governments in the same Capitol building.
Then the president, Ulysses Grant, refused to send troops.
Davis walked out.
Here is where most people get this story *backwards*.
The Democrats who took over in 1874 called themselves the *Redeemers*.
They wrote a new state constitution in 1876, still the Constitution of
Texas today, and built a party that would run Texas for more than 100
years, and that party was openly committed to white political control.
